questions.q: What direction did God give Adam and Eve in Paradise?
options: They could eat freely from anywhere.
Do not speak to the angels
Eat freely, but do not approach this tree
questions.rationale: ‘Live with your wife in Paradise and eat freely from it anywhere you may wish. Yet do not approach this tree lest you become wrongdoers.’

questions.q: From which Arabic word is ‘Islam’ derived, implying peace?
options: All its teachings are based directly or indirectly on peace.
questions.rationale: The very word Islam (from the Arabic silm) implies peace.

questions.q: What do plastic flowers lack, like the absurd forms of religiosity the article describes?
options: They look just like the real thing.
They look just like the real thing.
The fragrance of the real thing
They look grand but lack the spirit.
questions.rationale: If you smell a plastic flower, it has none of the fragrance of a real flower.

questions.q: Whom did the three companions ask about the Prophet’s worship?
options: The Prophet was not at home.
questions.rationale: The Prophet was not present at the time, so they asked his wives how he worshipped.

questions.q: What is the original meaning of jihad?
options: From juhd – to strive, to exert oneself to the utmost.
The article gives striving as the original meaning.
The article gives striving as the original meaning.
The article gives striving as the original meaning.
questions.rationale: Thus the original meaning of jihad is striving very hard.

questions.q: What does the article say about anger in itself?
options: It is not an evil; it becomes evil when allowed to go unchecked
The only solution is to control it.
The article says it is natural.
The article says to control it.
The article says it sours them.
questions.rationale: Anger is a natural phenomenon, and the only solution is to control it. Anger in itself is not an evil.

questions.article: Prophet of Peace, or of Violence
questions.q: How does the article define Islam?
options: A system of beliefs and ethics, not the behaviour of a group
The acts of some ‘Muslims’ do not define it.
The article does not say this.
The article does not say this.
questions.rationale: Islam is not the name given to the behaviour or the actions of a particular group of people who call themselves ‘Muslims’. Islam is a system of beliefs and ethics.

questions.q: To what role does the word ‘witness’ (shaheed) in verse 2: 143 refer?
options: The article explains it as dawah.
The role of Muslims as dayees
The role of judges in court
The article explains it as dawah.
The article explains it as dawah.
questions.rationale: The word witness (shaheed) in this verse refers to the role of Muslims as dayee’s.

questions.q: According to the verse quoted, what would have happened had the Prophet been harsh and hard-hearted?
options: They would have feared God more
This is not in the verse.
His people would have deserted him
It was by God’s grace that he was gentle.
The verse says they would have deserted him.
They would have obeyed more readily
The verse says they would have deserted him.
questions.rationale: If you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would surely have deserted you — so bear with them and pray for forgiveness for them.
